title: Doubtful forms of mobile animals are rare within a country but common between areas

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Doubtful forms of mobile animals are rare within a country but common between areas

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Among highly locomotive animals that unite for each birth, doubtful forms ranked as species by some and varieties by others are rarely found within the same country but are common in separated areas.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Amongst animals which unite for each birth, and which are highly locomotive, doubtful forms, ranked by one zoologist as a species and by another as a variety, can rarely be found within the same country, but are common in separated areas.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter II, “Variation under Nature”; section “Doubtful species”. Scope: highly mobile sexually reproducing animals such as birds and insects

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch02-03: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.73

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Occurrence and taxonomic resources provide broad coverage, and the spatial comparison is straightforward after defining disputed forms. Curating disagreement is required but feasible within sampled clades.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Classify taxonomically disputed forms among highly mobile sexual animals and compare their frequency in sympatric versus geographically separated pairs, controlling study effort. A substantially lower within-country frequency supports the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Taxonomic disagreement is not encoded uniformly.

Country boundaries are a historical proxy for separation.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.69
data adequacy: 0.65
operationalizability: 0.72
analysis feasibility: 0.73
data existence: 0.84

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Range products and checklists make a sympatry-versus-allopatry test practical for birds and some other mobile vertebrates. Doubtful rank has to be proxied by subspecies status or checklist conflict, and insects remain thinly and unevenly digitized. Sampling effort and taxonomic fashion can create the geographic pattern, so the result would be informative with a serious bias correction rather than decisive on its own.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Score taxa whose rank is disputed between species and variety, restrict the set to highly mobile animals that mate to reproduce, and compare how often those forms are sympatric within one country versus allopatric across separated areas. The pattern would be supported if doubtful forms were disproportionately allopatric in that group relative to sessile organisms; a similar rate of sympatric doubtful forms would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
'Doubtful' is a property of taxonomic disagreement, which tracks how thoroughly a group has been studied.

Political borders are an imperfect stand-in for Darwin's 'same country'.

Birds are well mapped and insects are not, so the mobile-animal scope is unevenly covered.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

operationalizability: 0.66
data adequacy: 0.48
analysis feasibility: 0.58
discriminating power: 0.52
